TIL that in the 1920s, "balloon jumping" was a popular fad where people harnessed themselves to small helium balloons to leap hundreds of feet over fields and buildings, until a series of lethal accidents ended the trend.
TIL that Elvis Presley did 636 sold out shows in Las Vegas and never once performed his song “Viva Las Vegas”
TIL that the ancient Chinese philosopher Confucius was willing to teach anyone who was eager to learn, asking for nothing more than a simple bundle of dried meat/jerky in exchange.

TIL the fruit thrown to Sylvester Stallone during Rocky's famous running montage was completely unscripted—a real street vendor in Philadelphia's Italian Market spontaneously tossed it to him while the crew was filming guerrilla-style.

TIL that until 2019, the international kilogram was defined by a metal cylinder kept near Paris. Even if the cylinder physically gained or lost mass, it was still exactly one kilogram by definition. Its official copies drifted by an average of about 50 micrograms relative to it over a century.

TIL when Calvin Coolidge was sworn in by his father at their family farmhouse in Vermont in 1923, he did not place his hand on a Bible. Although a family Bible was on the table, he did not use it, reflecting a New England Puritan tradition against swearing in on scripture.

TIL that The Nutcracker in 3D is the worst-rated Christmas movie on Rotten Tomatoes with a score of 0%. Roger Ebert described it a "wretched" and warned that it "may send children screaming under their seats." It was a box-office bomb, grossing $20 million against a $90 million budget.
TIL owning a pet rabbit is illegal in Queensland, Australia, where rabbits have been a destructive invasive species since being introduced in the 19th century.
TIL the city of Dish, Texas was originally named Clark. In 2005, the city accepted an offer from Dish Network to rename the city in exchange for all residents receiving free cable.
TIL that Chicago's nickname; The Windy City was not named after the heavy breezes that come from Lake Michigan but rather as a term to mock politicians who were "hot air."
